q: What does primary data share mean on a product carbon footprint, and how high should mine be?
title: Primary data share, explained
short: Primary data share is the percentage of your product footprint, in kg CO2e, calculated from data specific to your product's own processes and suppliers rather than industry averages. PACT asks for it but sets no pass mark. Buyers look for it to rise year by year, and supplier footprints for big materials raise it fastest.
audience: Suppliers filling PACT or Catena-X PCF templates

p: Add the emissions from every input calculated with primary data, divide by the total footprint, and multiply by 100. It is weighted by emissions, not by the number of data points, so one large input matters more than many small ones.

ul: Your own measured activity: kWh from your electricity bills, litres or kg of fuel from invoices, even when multiplied by a published factor such as the CEA grid factor.
A supplier's own footprint for the material they sell you, calculated for their product.
Not primary: a database average for steel, resin or cotton, or a spend-based estimate.

p: PACT and the Catena-X PCF Rulebook ask you to report it, without a fixed minimum. For a converter, raw materials often make up most of the footprint, so your own energy data alone gives a low share. Getting your two or three biggest suppliers to send their own figures is what moves it past half.

ul: Counting database factors for purchased materials as primary.
Reporting 100% when only your own energy was measured and materials were left out.
Leaving the field blank. Buyers read a blank as zero.

example.title: Worked example: one machined part (illustrative figures)
lines: Own plant energy from bills: 1.2 kg CO2e; steel: 3.0 kg; paint 0.3 kg; packaging 0.1 kg; total 4.6 kg CO2e
Steel from a database average: primary share = 1.2 / 4.6 = 26%
Steel figure from the mill's own product footprint: (1.2 + 3.0) / 4.6 = 91%
Same total, but one supplier's data lifts the share from 26% to 91%

senseible: Senseible builds Scope 1 and 2 figures from your plant's own electricity bills and fuel invoices, which count as primary activity data for those inputs. Supplier invoices for materials go to a separate Scope 3 evidence trail.
